transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-21 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Evan Rhodes (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Nina Soto (Redwood Partnerships), Derek Alvarez (Sentinel Head of Platform), Priya Kapoor (VP Partnerships), Jamal Rivera (Security Architect), Fiona Lee (GTM Ops)

Auto-summary: Quick alignment call to set the pilot guardrails and resolve security gating items; confirmed Redwood would run a targeted benchmark and provide partner enablement materials.

[00:00] Evan Rhodes: All right, hey everyone thanks for joining. we wanted to be mindful of time — i'll do a 2 minute kickoff then hand to maya for the tech plan.
[00:18] Derek Alvarez: yeah thanks evan. appreciate you squeezing us in. we're excited to see how this could shave down inference costs for our agent workloads.
[00:27] Maya Chen: cool hi folks. quick overview, i'm Maya, platform SE. we'll propose a two-model bench — a smaller open 7b-ish baseline and our quantized Redwood-optimized variant to show delta on latency and token cost.
[00:43] Priya Kapoor: just to scope expectations: sentinel wants a partner rev share but also clear SSO and co-marketing rules. we want clear logos and a joint case study if the pilot goes well.
[00:55] Nina Soto: totally — we'll include a partner playbook. evan i'll send the high level co-sell template after this.
[01:05] Jamal Rivera: quick sec on security: we use tenant isolation and strict KMS policies, need to understand how keys are managed in Redwood private vs hosted. do you have an hsm flow?
[01:18] Maya Chen: yes, good question. RedwoodPrivate supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations, but for the hosted flow we offer envelope encryption and a managed KMS. i'll put the exact diagram in the doc, but short answer: both paths supported but private gives you full key custody.
[01:36] Fiona Lee: are there audit logs at the route level? our compliance requires per-route traceability for three months.
[01:45] Evan Rhodes: yep per-route logs are available as an add-on retention; we can map that to your retention policy. nina will include link to the logs SLA in the follow up.
[01:55] Derek Alvarez: sounds ok. costs — can the benchmark reflect production batch sizes? we push wide parallelism and big sequences.
[02:05] Maya Chen: absolutely, include your p95 arrival and the longest sequence lengths. we'll mirror the batch distribution and run both streaming and non-streaming latencies.
[02:17] Priya Kapoor: commercial ask — we generally need a partner discount for logos and co-sell commitment, what's your standard?
[02:26] Evan Rhodes: we have a partner band that scales with committed spend and logos. i'll share the matrix but ballpark is 15-25% on committed reserved capacity; details in the deck.
[02:36] Jamal Rivera: another security point — do you support SAML SSO + SCIM for user provisioning?
[02:42] Nina Soto: yes SAML + SCIM; RBAC is configurable. we'll include admin role mapping examples in the playbook.
[02:51] Fiona Lee: timeline — can we do an 8-week pilot? week 1 onboarding, 2-4 benchmarks and tuning, 5-7 integration, 8 signoff.
[03:02] Maya Chen: that's realistic. we'll propose concrete milestones in the sample plan.
[03:10] Derek Alvarez: ok i want to flag a potential blocker — data residency. some of our EU customers require data to stay in EU zones. how does private deployment look for us?
[03:22] Evan Rhodes: Redwood Private can be deployed into your VPC or on-prem; we also support region pinning in hosted for EU-only processing. we'll map options and costs.
[03:33] Priya Kapoor: what's the fallback policy if a model variant is throttled? we need graceful degradation to a cheaper model not latency spike.
[03:44] Maya Chen: smart routing + automatic fallback is built-in; policy based routing can prefer low-cost variants and fall back to higher-capacity ones. we'll show an example YAML policy in the doc.
[03:57] Jamal Rivera: please spell out how KV cache is handled — i sometimes see notes saying KV cash in other docs (laughs)
[04:05] Maya Chen: yeah transcription sometimes writes KV cash; we'll clarify it's KV cache and how it's ephemeral per connection unless you enable prefix caching.
[04:15] Evan Rhodes: okay we'll pivot to the bench plan — maya, can you walk through the exact steps you'll run?
[04:22] Maya Chen: sure. step 1: ingest a representative prompt set (fiona will share). step 2: run two model variants across three regions (us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1) capturing p50/p95/p99 latency, cost per 1k tokens, and decode throughput. step 3: test typical production patterns: streaming, function calls, and longer context. step 4: provide a regression matrix for quality metrics.
[04:49] Fiona Lee: i'll share a sanitized prompt sample and traffic distribution by EOD.
[04:55] Derek Alvarez: on quality, we need to ensure quantization doesn't impact hallucination rate beyond x%. we'll need a QA checklist.
[05:03] Maya Chen: yes we'll include automated evals on your golden set and flag deltas; threshold configurable.
[05:12] Evan Rhodes: questions from our side — do you have any internal deadlines tied to Q1 budget approvals?
[05:18] Priya Kapoor: budget approval in mid-december; pilot needs to be underway before then for us to make a favorable case.
[05:26] Evan Rhodes: good to know. we'll aim to have benchmarks back before 2025-11-27 so you can present.
[05:33] Nina Soto: also to clarify marketing: we'll offer a joint press release template but co-marketing requires mutual sign-off; we can propose a timeline after pilot success.
[05:44] Derek Alvarez: ok, minor nit — latency SLO should be regional. can you include per-region SLOs?
[05:52] Maya Chen: yes per-region p95 targets are standard in our SLAs.
[05:58] Jamal Rivera: on audit logs, what's the tamper resistance? is it WORM or just retained logs?
[06:05] Evan Rhodes: we offer WORM options for enterprise retention plus tamper-evident checksums for compliance tiers. i'll put a note in the doc.
[06:14] Priya Kapoor: competitor question — some of our partners recommended Anthropic for safety controls. how does Redwood compare on safety tooling?
[06:24] Maya Chen: Redwood focuses on runtime controls and eval hooks; for safety filtering you can plug in third-party detectors or our builtin token filters. we'll include examples.
[06:34] Fiona Lee: can the pilot include a short workshop for our GTM and success teams?
[06:39] Nina Soto: yes we typically do a 2-hour enablement and a follow-up 90-min tech session. we'll propose dates.
[06:47] Derek Alvarez: commercial nuance — are there any minimum commitments for private deployment?
[06:53] Evan Rhodes: private tends to require a minimum reserved capacity because of the infra cost; for a pilot we can do a limited dedicated pool with short-term commit. details in pricing.
[07:02] Priya Kapoor: what about observability retention costs — long-term trace storage gets expensive and we need 18 month retention for some customers.
[07:10] Maya Chen: we recommend sampling + token-level aggregates for long retention, and raw traces on a shorter retention to keep costs predictable.
[07:18] Fiona Lee: thanks — that approach should work.
[07:22] Evan Rhodes: quick check — are there any absolute deal stoppers we should know about?
[07:26] Derek Alvarez: only data residency or an inability to plug our KMS; otherwise this is a go.
[07:32] Jamal Rivera: i want to see SOC2 artifact and any recent penetration test results.
[07:37] Nina Soto: we'll attach SOC2 report and recent pentest summary; if you need full artifacts we'll route through our security team and NDA channel.
[07:47] Fiona Lee: ok, let's confirm dates — if you can run the bench this week and share results by 11/27, we can prep pilot comms for the mid-dec budget meeting.
[07:58] Maya Chen: we'll start ingesting the sample once fiona shares the prompts; should be doable.
[08:05] Evan Rhodes: wrap up — i'll send the partner playbook, pricing bands, and the enablement calendar. maya will own the bench and results. jamal will get the security packet. nina and priya will confirm GTM milestones.
[08:22] Derek Alvarez: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[08:25] Priya Kapoor: thanks, talk soon.
[08:28] [call ends]

Notes on transcript: occasional mis-hearings corrected inline (e.g., KV cache spelled as KV cash in earlier notes); some speaker labels approximated when speakers talk over each other.
